methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Virginia's AI challenge isn't data centers. It's small-business adoption | Guest column - Richmond Times-Dispatch
signals.signal_reading: Guest column highlights that Virginia's AI infrastructure investment (data centers) is disconnected from small business capability—signaling that neither depth nor distribution of AI adoption is occurring at the business level despite proximity to AI infrastructure.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches AI training program for workplace professionals - WDBJ7
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College launching workplace AI training in a non-metro region signals potential for distributed capability building through local institutions, moving beyond platform adoption toward hands-on professional fluency outside the NoVA corridor.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free community AI workshops in Hampton Roads represent grassroots peer-network knowledge transfer—exactly the 'broad fluency through distributed networks' model that characterizes deep, distributed adoption rather than platform-dependent usage.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU partnership with AI Ready RVA concentrates advanced AI education and innovation resources in the Richmond metro hub, potentially deepening capability in a secondary urban center while leaving rural areas unaddressed.

signals.title: Experts+foresee+legal+malpractice+risk+for+those+who+eschew+AI - Virginia Lawyers Weekly
signals.signal_reading: Legal profession facing malpractice risk for not using AI suggests pressure toward shallow platform adoption driven by liability rather than deep technical understanding—widespread but surface-level integration across Virginia's legal sector.
